purpose: Ingest sparse-state discoveries spanning cryptographic timing, kernel lifecycle, malicious-file handling, real-world AI evaluation, biological material custody, reproducible simulation, LLM container supply-chain security and laboratory-code interoperability.

source_ingestion_policy.rule: Every substantive unique publication, dataset, advisory, standard, code system, material record, software resource or information item receives a Worldshepherd use when it materially improves any capability, or an explicit negative-control role.
source_ingestion_policy.duplicates: NVD/CVE/vendor mirrors, publisher/version-of-record copies and material-record mirrors for the same underlying item are provenance aliases and are not independent evidence.
source_ingestion_policy.search_noise: CVE, article, catalog and laboratory-code identifiers can materially improve Worldshepherd while carrying zero automatic Glob evidence; they never promote a target without independently verified physical data.

sources.title: CVE-2026-40194 — phpseclib variable-time HMAC comparison
sources.note: Use as a timing-side-channel regression test: cryptographic authentication comparisons should use constant-time primitives and timing tests should scale input repetitions enough to reveal measurable differences. 40194 is the CVE identifier.

sources.title: CVE-2025-40194 — Linux intel_pstate QoS request lifecycle defect
sources.note: Use as an object-lifetime/reference-release ordering case in hot-remove/error paths. 40194 is the CVE identifier.

sources.title: From Validation to Real-World Impact: Educational Effectiveness of an AI-Powered Medical History-Taking System
sources.note: Use propensity-score matching and opt-in real-world adoption analysis as a precedent for evaluating AI systems after technical validation under nonrandom operational uptake. 89367 is the article identifier.

sources.title: ATCC 95067 — yWXD452 human clone
sources.note: Use lot/certificate, contamination and handling metadata as another governed physical-asset custody pattern. 95067 is the catalog identifier.

sources.title: ATCC 92453 — yWXD5193 human clone
sources.note: Use BSL, certificate and GenBank cross-reference metadata as a provenance/interoperability pattern for governed research assets. 92453 is the catalog identifier.

sources.title: Emergence of alternative stable states in microbial communities undergoing horizontal gene transfer
sources.note: Use alternative-stable-state modeling and the linked archived simulation code as a reproducibility/control example for nonlinear multistate systems. 99593 is the article identifier.

sources.title: CVE-2026-54232 — vLLM dependency confusion in Docker build
sources.note: Use as a software-supply-chain control: custom indexes plus --extra-index-url/unsafe best-match can permit dependency confusion and root execution during image builds. Fixed in vLLM 0.22.1. 54232 is the CVE identifier.

sources.title: CVE-2025-54232 — Adobe FrameMaker use-after-free
sources.note: Use malicious-document parsing as an untrusted-file-ingestion hardening case. 54232 is the CVE identifier.

sources.title: CVE-2026-33295 — AVideo stored XSS in CDN download buttons
sources.note: Use JavaScript-string/context-aware output encoding as a UI security test case. 33295 is the CVE identifier.

sources.title: LOINC 33295-7 — JC Virus PCR, CSF
sources.authority: LOINC-exposed laboratory interoperability metadata via Mayo Clinic Laboratories
sources.note: Use stable external-code plus local-order/result-ID separation as an interoperability pattern for Worldshepherd measurement schemas. 33295 is part of a LOINC code, not a physical Glob value.

information_updates.finding: CVE-2026-54232 provides a direct AI-infrastructure supply-chain precedent: unregistered package names combined with an extra package index and unsafe best-match selection allowed a public-index package to win resolution and execute as root during a container build.
information_updates.claims_boundary: Apply as a build-policy test pattern; no claim is made that current Worldshepherd uses vLLM or the affected index strategy until repository/runtime inventory confirms it.

information_updates.finding: The 2026 AMTES study separates technical feasibility from real-world educational effectiveness under voluntary adoption and uses matched observational analysis. Worldshepherd AI evaluation should similarly distinguish bench accuracy from realized operational benefit and adoption bias.
information_updates.claims_boundary: Methodological transfer only; clinical/educational effect sizes are not generalized to Worldshepherd.

information_updates.finding: LOINC-style separation between stable external semantic codes and local order/result identifiers is a useful pattern for Worldshepherd measurement interoperability: preserve canonical concept identity while retaining local instrument/channel/source identifiers.
information_updates.claims_boundary: Schema-design inference from laboratory interoperability practice, not a claim of LOINC applicability to all Worldshepherd domains.

next_actions: Continue analyzer-driven sparse-state internet scans and reduce the count of single-record/single-namespace states while preserving all prior observations.
Check the actual Worldshepherd dependency and image-build configuration for vLLM, extra-index-url, unsafe-best-match, phpseclib and similar patterns before assigning remediation status.
Use longitudinal/observational AI effectiveness and reproducible nonlinear-simulation sources as validation-method inputs independent of number collisions.
Continue same-system physical topology and relational verification with fixed tolerance and experiment-wide multiple-testing/false-discovery controls.
